answer: A registry can make each new identity cost more than the last: the first registration is cheap, but the fee and refundable bond rise steeply with every additional vertex one operator controls, so a Sybil farm faces a basalt-hard cost curve instead of a flat price. A challenger who proves duplication can push the offender off the ridge, forfeiting its bonds and reputation, while honest single agents keep their deposit and keep working. Duplication then stops paying for itself.
